items.title: Personality matters most in the consulting room
items.body: The finding that different traits suit different work applies to clinical AI. A scribe should be accurate and plain; a patient-facing assistant needs warmth without sycophancy. The GPT-4o episode, where users grieved a retired model and one said it did more than any therapy, is a reminder that people form attachments to chatbots, and that a patient-facing tool can feel supportive while being wrong.

items.title: Sycophancy is a safety issue
items.body: The host notes that a flattering model is of dubious value for work that needs pushback. In clinical reasoning, a tool that agrees with the user's first impression is dangerous. Test any decision-support tool by presenting it with a wrong assumption and seeing whether it corrects you.

items.title: Chinese models in government
items.body: DHS has banned DeepSeek from federal systems, which the host calls a signal and not a security finding. For the NHS, supplier due diligence should look at where a tool is hosted and who can access the data, whatever the model's origin.
